applicable_when: The kernel performs a layout transposition: input in_ptr0 has stride (290400,1,5280,96) — NHWC-like with channel stride=1 — while output out_ptr0 has stride (290400,3025,55,1) — NCHW. The load index is y0 + 96*x2 + 290400*y1 where x2 is the XBLOCK (spatial) dimension and y0 is the channel dimension. Within a warp, threads share the same y0 (YBLOCK=8 means y varies slowly) and differ in x2 (XBLOCK=128). This means loads from in_ptr0 are strided by 96 between consecutive threads — highly uncoalesced. L2 is saturated at 96.79% and 41.4% of stalls are L1TEX waits. Adding tl.max_contiguous and tl.multiple_of hints on the load pointer offsets tells the Triton compiler that the access pattern is contiguous and aligned, enabling 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads instead of scalar loads. Autotuning YBLOCK=96 would make the channel dimension perfectly tile-aligned, eliminating modulo/divide overhead and making loads from in_ptr0 fully coalesced.
